title: When I need to track my reputation or performance metrics across platforms, I want to automatically
job_to_be_done: When I need to track my reputation or performance metrics across platforms, I want to automatically export and visualize historical data, so I can analyze trends without manual data entry.
painful_workflow: Tracking reputation changes over time across multiple sites by manually recording daily or weekly reputation points because the built-in history is not easily exportable.
current_workaround: Users copy-paste data from the reputation tab into spreadsheets or use third-party scripts (e.g., Stack Exchange Data Explorer queries) to pull history.

competitors.name: Stack Exchange Data Explorer (SEDE)
competitors.notes: Official Stack Exchange tool allowing SQL queries to extract reputation history per user. Requires technical SQL knowledge. No visualization or automated exporting — users must manually run queries and export results. Powerful but not user-friendly; no scheduling, no aggregation across sites in one click. Significant friction for non-technical users.
competitors.feature_overlap: Historical reputation data extraction, multi-site querying possible via UNION, CSV export
competitors.market_positioning: Query tool for power users, not a dedicated tracking/visualization product

competitors.name: Stack Exchange API
competitors.notes: Official API provides reputation history endpoints. Requires programming knowledge to build a tracker. Not a product — infrastructure. Users building scripts around this are evidence of unmet need, not a competing solution.
competitors.feature_overlap: Raw reputation history endpoint, programmatic access

competitors.name: StackExchange™ Super User Widget (iOS)
competitors.notes: iOS app with widgets showing current reputation across SE sites. Provides at-a-glance monitoring but no historical trending, no export, no analytics. Read-only current-snapshot display. Limited to iOS. Last updated appears inactive or minimally maintained.
competitors.market_positioning: Mobile widget for quick reputation checks

competitors.name: StackStatus (GitHub project)
competitors.notes: Various open-source scripts and repos for tracking SE reputation. Typically command-line scripts requiring local setup. No hosted SaaS, no historical visualization out of the box. Fragmented ecosystem of one-off scripts, not a product.
competitors.feature_overlap: Basic reputation fetching, sometimes CSV output

competitors.name: Stack Exchange Reputation Tracker (various userscripts)
competitors.notes: StackApps hosts multiple user scripts that add reputation graphs to profile pages. Examples: 'Stack Exchange Reputation Graph' userscript. Browser-dependent, no cross-device sync, no export, no persistent external storage. Fragile — breaks on SE UI updates.

competitors.name: Google Sheets / Excel (manual tracking)
competitors.notes: Users manually record reputation points daily/weekly. Extremely high friction, error-prone, time-consuming. Evidence from source (SIG-002) confirms this is the painful workaround people resort to. Not a product competitor but the status quo behavior a product must displace.

competitors.name: GitHub contribution graph trackers (adjacent category)
competitors.notes: Products like GitHub Skyline, GitHub Readme Stats, etc. demonstrate demand for personal developer metric visualization. None of these track Stack Exchange reputation — they focus on GitHub contributions. However, they validate that developers value quantified reputation/contribution visualization. No cross-platform aggregation.

competitors.name: Readme Stats / Profile Summary generators
competitors.notes: Tools that generate GitHub profile stats cards. Some include Stack Overflow reputation badges (static, current only). Not a history tracker or analytics tool. Validates desire to display SE reputation elsewhere, but not the JTBD of tracking trends.

competitors.name: Dev.to / Hashnode built-in analytics
competitors.notes: Developer blogging platforms with built-in analytics for posts. Overlapping audience (developers who write), but focuses on content performance, not Stack Exchange reputation. Demonstrates developer-writer interest in metrics.

competitors.name: Shields.io badges
competitors.notes: Can display Stack Exchange reputation as a badge. Static, current-value only. No history, no export, no analytics. Used in README profiles.

substitutes: GitHub profile stats tools with SE badges (static only)
verified_facts: The cluster is supported by exactly one signal (SIG-002) from one source (SRC-002) of one type (forum), per independent_sources=1 and source_type_count=1.
The evidence text in SIG-002 describes manual tracking behavior and contains no complaint language, frequency data, or quantified impact.
The cluster's stated workaround relies on free tooling: spreadsheets and Stack Exchange Data Explorer queries.
inferences: Reputation is a discretionary gamification metric; users tracking it manually are likely doing so out of personal interest, not operational necessity.
Because free programmatic options (SEDE, per the cluster's workaround field) already exist, the residual pain after using available free tools is likely minimal.
The 'daily or weekly' cadence in the painful_workflow description is likely an overstatement tailored to justify the cluster rather than an observed pattern.
assumptions: That manual reputation recording is burdensome enough that users want it automated — asserted by the cluster, not evidenced by SIG-002.
That a meaningful population of Stack Exchange users performs this manual tracking at all.
That the JTBD's 'across platforms' framing extends beyond Stack Exchange, which the single Stack Exchange-only signal does not support.
unknowns: How many users actually engage in manual reputation tracking.
The actual time cost per week of the manual workflow.
Whether any user has ever paid money for reputation analytics or export tooling.
Whether existing free scripts/API-based solutions already fully satisfy the need.
Any demographic or segment data on who these power users are and whether they have budget.
